ai.description: This stout viper reaches 1.5m. It is grey or brown with darker, rectangular dorsal blotches and a broad, triangular head. A distinct row of small scales separates the eye from the upper lip.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Levantine Viper is distinguished by a series of large, dark, blotch-like markings along its back, which contrast sharply with the smaller, more uniform spotting of other vipers.
ai.habitat: The Levantine viper inhabits rocky, arid hillsides and scrublands in the Indian subcontinent, typically ranging from lowlands up to 2,500 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Levantine viper is primarily nocturnal during hot summer months, but shifts to diurnal activity in the spring and autumn to regulate its body temperature effectively.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Macrovipera lebetinus* is not native to India. It is oviparous, typically laying 8–20 eggs in summer, though it is often confused with other regional viper species.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Levantine Viper does not occur within the Indian subcontinent; its range is restricted to the Middle East, North Africa, and parts of Central Asia.
